_readme: How a browse-wall clip is driven. Keys are component slugs; `pnpm record:previews` plays each one against /preview/<slug> in a headless Chromium and encodes it to public/crafter/. Coordinates are in the captured 1280x960 frame; `t` is ms from the first recorded frame, and a NEGATIVE t plays the step during settle, before the camera rolls - that is how a clip opens on a state the component only reaches by being used. Every timeline must end where it began, because the loop is a hard jump-cut; `loop` records why that cut is invisible. `stage` lays the demo out for a narrower window and paints it across the full frame, zooming a component that would otherwise sit lost in whitespace at card size. `waitFor` is a JS expression polled until truthy before settle, for demos whose only repeatable frame is one they reach on their own clock. `lockTheme` records once in the named theme and hands the same file to both, for components that paint their own colours instead of the theme's.

arrow-tooltip.loop: Opens and closes with the pointer parked off the grid and every tooltip shut.
arrow-tooltip.note: Jump-cut moves (durationMs 0) on purpose: delayDuration is 0, so an eased path between triggers grazes neighbours and pops stray tooltips. The screencast draws no cursor, so nothing is lost. DOM order is Top, Left, Right, Bottom - nth 0,2,3,1 walks it clockwise. Recorded unscaled: this is the one component a `stage` zoom cannot help, because the tooltip is portalled to the body and placed by Floating UI off a measured rect, which any ancestor scale throws off by the scale factor - the tooltips end up nowhere near their triggers.

dynamic-island.loop: Mounts in `silent` and the last click returns it to `silent`, pointer back at its opening park, with ~1s of rest before the cut.
dynamic-island.note: Never bare text= for Ring/Timer/Silent - the pill renders those same words itself. Only the control strip wraps them in a <button>. Cancel is clicked from inside the timer state so the clip shows the component's own control working.

super-hover-list.loop: The pointer enters during settle and never leaves, so autoplay stays frozen for the whole take and the sweep returns to the row it started on.
super-hover-list.note: Covers are remote CDN URLs painted as background-image on hidden elements, hence the long settle. Autoplay's own period is ~66s - far past a clip - but onPointerEnter freezes it, so hovering is both the better beat and the only loopable one.

letter-reveal.loop: Letter arrival is a pure function of scroll progress with no latched state, so rewinding to 0 un-types every glyph back to the empty headline.
letter-reveal.note: No lockTheme any more: the demo used to force a bg-black panel while the components own caption and hairline read from theme tokens, so light mode was unreadable and only a dark take was usable. The demo now passes no surface override, the component paints bg-background/text-foreground, and each theme gets its own real recording. The -1800 return deliberately overshoots so it clamps at 0 whatever the panel height resolves to.

countdown-timer.loop: Opens and closes on the same rest state - 0:33, paused - because the pre-roll reset and the closing reset leave identical frames, with 1.4s of settled numerals before the cut.
countdown-timer.note: The demo mounts with autoStart loop and a 33s cycle, far too long to record. The pre-roll reset pauses it so the clip can open at rest; [aria-label="Start timer"] only resolves once it is paused. Five NumberFlow rolls (33 down to 28) is the beat.

username-reel.loop: Exactly one 7350ms cycle (4500 spin + 850 land + 2000 delay), started inside the 1.5s rest window, so the last frame is the same landed handle the first shows.
username-reel.note: No input: the demo passes `loop` and drives itself. Where the clip STARTS is the whole game - the reel re-shuffles its names every cycle, so mid-spin frames never repeat and only the rest frame is stable. waitFor catches the moment the non-final rows drop to opacity 0, and the settle lands the camera in the middle of the window.

handwritten-response.loop: Recording starts after the mount-time write has finished, so frame 0 is the completed sentence; the click rewrites the identical text (done by 5700ms) and the cursor is off the button by 2000ms.
handwritten-response.note: The 4500ms write is exact - the component charges pen time per character, 125 units at 0.036s. The settle must not be shortened: it covers the dynamic chunk, the Caveat webfont from Google Fonts (network required, or the handwriting falls back to a system sans and the clip is pointless) and the entrance write, which does not loop.

hero-carousel.loop: Uncontrolled with defaultIndex 4, and the last click returns focus to that same card, so headline, filmstrip geometry, accent grade and the 05/09 rail all land back where frame 0 had them.
hero-carousel.note: Nothing advances on its own - autoplay defaults off, so the clicks are required. Only the nine strip buttons carry aria-labels, so each title is unique. Do not scroll: the stage has a non-passive wheel listener that would step the strip. The closing park matters as much as the clicks: the final click leaves the pointer on a strip card, and a hovered card expands and shifts its neighbours, so without it the last frame's filmstrip sits a card-width off the first frame's. The hero photo runs a 6s linear Ken-Burns (scale 1.42 -> 1.28) that RESTARTS whenever the active card changes, so the loop is only seamless if both ends sit at the same point of that zoom. The pre-roll clicks away and back to restart it, and settleMs is set so frame 0 is the same distance past a restart as the final frame is past the closing click. Clicking the already-active card would not restart it, hence two pre-roll clicks rather than one.

works-wheel.loop: The closing -3600 is clamped by the component to exactly turn 0, collapsing the drum back into the resting ring with 1.3s of easing headroom before the cut.
works-wheel.note: WHEEL_UNITS is 900, so each 900 is exactly one item, and only the sum of a gesture matters. Gaps are kept at 400ms+ because a 140ms quiet window fires SETTLE, which snaps to the nearest item - firing inside it would snap mid-glide. Real wheel events only: the page never scrolls, the component just reads deltaY.

glass-lens-carousel.loop: Three panels out and three panels back, so the row rests on the same panel - Prismatic Rift, 01/09 - at both ends, with the cursor parked in the bottom-right corner throughout.
glass-lens-carousel.note: Two things this recipe is tuned against, both invisible in a still. (1) The pre-roll is the clip run once with the camera off. The rows resting state straight after mount is NOT the state it comes back to after a gesture - it is still drifting toward centre, and EASE 0.09 / SNAP_EASE 0.05 make that drift outlast any settle worth waiting through - so frame 0 has to be a post-gesture state, not a post-mount one. (2) The return is 3600 against an outbound of 2700 because the row does not deliver a gesture symmetrically: the same magnitude going back lands a panel short every time, so the numbers are deliberately unequal - matching them is the bug, not the fix. The cursor must also sit over the canvas for the non-passive wheel listener to see the event at all; the corner is chosen because no panel is picked there.

dither-helix-carousel.loop: Four slots out, four slots back, and the drum snaps to a whole slot - so the same card faces front at both ends, with the cursor returned to the corner and every card back at full dither.
dither-helix-carousel.note: 1818px is exactly 4 slots at WHEEL 0.0022. Settle must clear ENTRY_SPIN_MS (2400) plus the staggered per-card entry, or the clip opens mid-arrival. The mid-clip hover is the components signature - pointing at a card clears its dither and pushes the rest back - and it is safe to loop because the pointer leaves again before the cut.

molten-ring-carousel.loop: Three slots out, three slots back at the same delta, so the ring snaps home to the card it started facing. Surface tension falls to zero at rest, so both ends are the same perfectly smooth ring.
molten-ring-carousel.note: 1364px is 3 slots at WHEEL 0.0022. Travel is what makes the cards fuse and part into strands; the pointer sweep between the two gestures is the other half of the component - it widens the fusion radius under itself - and it ends parked back in the corner so the closing frame carries no pointer influence. The long tail after the last gesture is not padding: SNAP_EASE is 0.06 and surface tension only falls to zero once the ring is genuinely at rest, so a shorter clip cuts while the strands are still contracting.

spine-accordion.loop: Ends on the same spine the demo opens with (defaultIndex 7) and parks the cursor back off-stage, so the cut lands on the resting frame.
spine-accordion.note: Jump-cut moves (durationMs 0): hover opens a panel, so an eased path across the shelf cascades every spine it grazes and the unfurl never finishes. Each dwell is longer than the 700ms flex-basis transition so the picture settles before the next move. Coordinates come from the button rects, which shift as panels open - hence selector+nth rather than x/y.

mercury-dial.loop: Opens, is browsed, and closes again - the last frame is the resting circle the first frame shows, cursor parked off-stage so no hover disc is lit.
mercury-dial.note: Recorded unscaled: the grab converts pointer pixels into the component's own 32px units through its `size` prop, and a `stage` zoom is a second transform it cannot see. The trigger is picked by aria-controls, not aria-haspopup - the preview page's own theme control answers to that too, and pressing it reads to the component as an outside press. NO GRAB STEP: a press-drag-release is correct under real CDP input (verified open, closed, and after a hover walk - the click is suppressed every time and nothing toggles) but does not reproduce inside the recorder, where it leaks a click and opens the menu a beat early. The clip therefore shows open, hover and close only; the stretch is the one thing here a clip does not carry.
